lines.japanese: というわけで地道に働くことを選んだ俺は、昨日と同じ現場を訪ねて（ちゃんと開始１５分前に入ったんだぞ）その末席に加えていただいた。
lines.english: And so, having chosen the honest path of steady work, I returned to yesterday's site—fifteen full minutes before the shift began, mind you—and was graciously admitted at the very bottom of the ranks.

lines.japanese: 高速道路の橋脚補強工事は一日や二日じゃ終わらない。しばらくはここの世話になるべきだろうか。
lines.english: Reinforcing the expressway piers would take more than a day or two. Maybe I ought to keep working here for a while.

lines.japanese: であれば、なんとか周囲を騙し騙しやり通さなくちゃならない。夜の陰で作業着に着替えながら、俺はボクサーショーツの緒を締めなおした。
lines.english: If I did, I’d have to keep bluffing my way past everybody somehow. As I changed into my work clothes under cover of darkness, I cinched the cord of my boxer shorts and braced myself anew.

lines.japanese: 「成田。おまえ、毎日来る気あんだったら、事務のババアに電話して正規の手続き踏んどけよ。他のバイトと同じ働きで、日給に差があるなんて馬鹿らしいだろ」
lines.english: “Narita. If you plan on coming every day, call the old woman in the office and get yourself registered properly. It's stupid to do the same work as the other temps for less pay.”

lines.japanese: ヒゲ監督のありがたいお言葉。でも、俺ひとりで決められることじゃない。鷲介にだって言い分はある。
lines.english: Words of wisdom from Beard Boss. But it wasn't mine alone to decide. Shu had a say in it too.

lines.japanese: 俺がヘルメットをかぶって聞こえないふりをしていると、おっさんは呆れたように鼻を鳴らした。そして、
lines.english: I pulled on my hard hat and pretended not to hear. The man snorted in exasperation. Then—

lines.japanese: 「フラフラしてねえで社会の責任しょえっつってんだよ小僧」
lines.english: “Quit drifting around and shoulder some goddamn responsibility, kid.”

lines.japanese: 聞こえよがしな独り言を漏らしながら持ち場へ戻っていった。
lines.english: He muttered it just loudly enough for me to hear and returned to his post.

lines.japanese: 俺は無意識のうちに後ろ頭をがしがし……掻こうとして、爪の先がＡＢＳ樹脂の硬い球面に滑って流れた。ああそうだ、たったいまヘルメットをかぶったばかりだ。
lines.english: Without thinking, I reached up to rake at the back of my head... and my fingernails skated across the hard dome of my ABS-plastic helmet. Oh, right. I'd just put it on.

lines.japanese: 仕方ない、代わりにベロでほっぺの裏でも突付いて遊ぼう。
lines.english: Fine. I'd just poke the inside of my cheek with my tongue for fun instead.

lines.japanese: つんつん、つんつん。
lines.english: Poke, poke. Poke, poke.

lines.japanese: わはは、こりゃおもしれーや。
lines.english: Hahaha. Now this was fun.
“Whew...”

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth.*

lines.japanese: それからの俺は、ひたすら精力的な労働に励んだ。
lines.english: After that, I threw myself tirelessly into the work.

lines.japanese: 俺はいつだって、仕事に対してだけは可能なかぎり真摯なんだ。ほんとほんと、これマジで。
lines.english: When it comes to work, I'm always as serious as I can be. Seriously. I'm not kidding about this.

lines.japanese: 可能なかぎりはな。
lines.english: As much as I can, anyway.

lines.japanese: 日付が変わり、そこからさらに何時間かが経過したころ──
lines.english: The date changed, and several more hours went by—

lines.japanese: ──ふと気付いたら、車線ふたつとガードレールを隔てた遠く歩道の上、四階建てビルを背に、片膝立てて座りこみする男の影があった。
lines.english: At some point, I looked up and found a man's silhouette sitting with one knee raised on the distant sidewalk beyond two lanes and a guardrail, his back to a four-story building.

lines.japanese: ダンプからこぼれる塵埃よりも鬱陶しい、時代錯誤な男のワンレン。森里だ。いつからいたんだろう。覚えがないのは作業に集中していた証拠。
lines.english: That anachronistic curtain of hair annoyed me more than dust off a dump truck. Morisato. How long had he been there? The fact I hadn't noticed proved how completely I'd been absorbed in my work.

lines.japanese: やつは俺の視線に気付くと、桜の樹の下の酔っぱらいみたいにやおら手を上げプラプラと振った。暗くてよく見えないけど、どうも口を閉じたまま笑ってるっぽい。
lines.english: When he noticed me looking, he slowly raised a hand and let it flap like some drunk beneath the cherry blossoms. It was too dark to see clearly, but he seemed to be smiling without opening his mouth.

lines.japanese: ひとの職場に来るなっつってんのに日本語の理解できないやつだ。俺はタチの悪い野犬を払うように、手の甲を二回突きだした。
lines.english: I'd told him not to come to my workplace, but apparently plain Japanese was beyond him. I thrust the back of my hand at him twice, shooing away a vicious stray dog.

lines.japanese: まぁまぁ──とでも言いたいのか、森里は座ったまま両てのひらを立てて対抗する。
lines.english: Easy, easy, he seemed to reply, raising both palms without getting up.

lines.japanese: どうやら立ちさるつもりはないが、昨日みたいにこっちへ近付いてくるつもりもないらしい。じゃあ何の用だ。休日前に意味もなく夜更かしがしたいんだろうか。
lines.english: Didn't look like he was leaving, but unlike yesterday, he wasn't coming any closer either. So what did he want? Was he just staying up late for no reason because tomorrow was a holiday?

lines.japanese: ともあれ他にどうしようもないので、とりあえず俺は、その髪の長い路傍の石を忘れることにした。
lines.english: There was nothing else I could do, so for the moment I decided to forget about that long-haired stone by the roadside.

lines.japanese: さいわい忘れるのは得意なんだ。
lines.english: Good thing I'm good at forgetting.

lines.japanese: 「ちぃーす」
lines.english: “Sup.”

lines.japanese: 休憩時間に歩道まで足を運んでみると、森里はいじくっていたケータイを畳みながら年寄りくさい動きで立ちあがった。
lines.english: When I walked over during my break, Morisato snapped shut the phone he'd been fiddling with and heaved himself up like an old man.

lines.japanese: パーカーの前が上までフルに閉めきられていて、ゆうべ刻みつけられた猛禽の傷跡は確認できなかった。
lines.english: His hoodie was zipped all the way to the top, hiding the raptor's claw marks carved into him last night.

lines.japanese: 「かかか、おもしれー。見てるだけでウケるわ、おまえ、めっちゃ真面目にやってんのな」
lines.english: “Kakaka, this is hilarious. Just watching you cracks me up. You're taking this insanely seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーよハゲ。見学するな。俺を見学するな」
lines.english: “Shut up, Baldy. Quit gawking. I'm not a tourist attraction.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、照れんなって。偉いって実際、あんだけの量の──」
lines.english: “No, no, don't get embarrassed. I'm honestly impressed. That whole huge pile of—”

lines.japanese: ぞろぞろと、メットを脱いだ若いやつらが俺のうしろを通りすぎていく。ニンニク禁止とか坦々麺バリ美味ぇとかはしゃいでる声が聞こえた。バイト仲間同士、みんな仲良くお夜食にでも行くんだろう。
lines.english: A bunch of young guys with their helmets off filed past behind me. I heard them getting excited about ‘no garlic’ and the dan dan noodles being crazy good. They were probably all going out for a late-night bite together.

lines.japanese: 関係ないやと思った。
lines.english: Nothing to do with me, I thought.

lines.japanese: 連中が歩きながらどこを見てたのかは知らない。森里はポケットに手を突っこんで、数秒のあいだ口笛でも吹くみたいにあさっての方角を向いていた。
lines.english: I had no idea where they were looking as they walked. Morisato shoved his hands into his pockets and spent several seconds looking pointedly off at nowhere in particular, as if whistling to himself.

lines.japanese: 「……え、成田は行かなくていいの」
lines.english: “...Uh, Narita, don't you need to go with them?”

lines.japanese: 陽気な声が遠のいたあとで、森里はラーメン屋目指して行軍する集団の背中を目で指した。
lines.english: Once the cheerful voices had faded, Morisato nodded toward the backs of the group marching toward the ramen shop.

lines.japanese: 「さあ。いんじゃね？」
lines.english: “Dunno. Guess not.”

lines.japanese: 誘われてねえし。
lines.english: Not like they'd invited me.

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんか悪いな、俺のせいで」
lines.english: “Ah. Sorry. My fault.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “Whatever.”

lines.japanese: っせえな、だから誘われてねえんだよ。おまえがいてもいなくても。
lines.english: Oh, shut up. I hadn’t been invited, whether he was here or not.

lines.japanese: 「つか、気持ち悪りぃな、その殊勝な態度。おまえ、きのう最後、俺にブチ切れてなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Besides, what's with the creepy contrite act? Weren't you furious with me at the end of last night?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なに、おまえまだそんなこと気にしてんの」
lines.english: “Huh? You're still worried about that?”

lines.japanese: 「俺じゃねーよ。俺はもともと１ミリもキレてねーよタコ」
lines.english: “I'm not. I wasn't angry by so much as a millimeter, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、いいじゃん。んな細けーコトいつまでも引きずんなよ」
lines.english: “Then we’re good. Don’t keep dragging every little thing out.”

lines.japanese: 「だから俺じゃねーつってんだろ。つかおまえ、ひとの職場に来んなつったよな、今日はなんだよ」
lines.english: “I just said I’m not the one hung up on it. And I told you not to come to my workplace. So what the hell do you want today?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうそうコレコレ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. This, this.”

lines.japanese: 森里は顎まで上がっていたジッパーを、すばやく胸あたりまで下ろした。ちらりと見えた首には、爪痕を隠すように包帯が巻きついていた。多少の哀れを催したが、俺は気付かなかったことにした。
lines.english: Morisato quickly pulled the zipper from his chin down to his chest. A bandage circled the strip of neck it exposed, hiding the claw marks. It stirred a faint trace of pity in me, which I decided not to notice.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、返しとくわ。いちおー」
lines.english: “Anyway, figured I’d give this back.”

lines.japanese: やつがふところから取りだしたのは、きっちり畳まれたモスグリーンのカラータオルだった。
lines.english: What he drew from inside his jacket was a neatly folded moss-green towel.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は怪訝さを表に出しながら受けとった。石鹸の香りが広がりそうな、ふっくらした手触り。ほんのりと森里の体温が移っていた。きもっ。
lines.english: I took it, making no effort to hide my suspicion. It was thick and soft, as though the scent of soap might bloom from it, and it still held a trace of Morisato's warmth. Gross.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。そういや俺、ゆうべこいつにタオルやったんだっけ。そんでわざわざ返しに来たってわけか、ご丁寧な。
lines.english: Oh, right. I'd given him a towel last night, hadn't I? And he'd come all this way to return it. Well, how very thoughtful of him.

lines.japanese: でもあれは、おんぼろモーテルの名前が入った平地付きのありふれた安物だ。こんな海外の一流ホテルに置いてありそうな高級品じゃない。
lines.english: But mine had been an ordinary cheapo with the name of some run-down motel printed across the woven band. Not some luxury item you'd find in a first-rate hotel overseas.

lines.japanese: 「え……いや、いいよ。いらねーよ。あれ貰いもんだし」
lines.english: “Uh... no, I'm good. Don't want it. Mine was free anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「あそ？　じゃあ捨てといて。んな、俺だって使わねーし」
lines.english: “Yeah? Then throw it out. Not like I'm gonna use it.”

lines.japanese: 捨てろ言われてもなあ……。
lines.english: He could tell me to throw it out, but still...

lines.japanese: 俺は軍手を外した埃っぽい手で、清潔な生地の一辺をつまんで持ちあげた。タイ料理屋のグリーンカレーみたいな色をしたタオルが、やる気なさげにだらりと垂れた。
lines.english: With a dusty hand freed from its work glove, I pinched one edge of the spotless fabric and lifted it. The towel, the color of green curry at a Thai restaurant, drooped limply from my fingers.

lines.japanese: たぶんこいつ自身もふっくらと生まれてきたからには、工事現場のプー太郎に手ぬぐい感覚で使われるのははなはだ遺憾であろう。
lines.english: A towel born this plush could hardly be pleased to end up serving as a common washcloth for some jobless bum on a construction site.

lines.japanese: 「これアレ？　親戚のおばちゃんがお中元で送ってきたとか？」
lines.english: “What is this? Something your aunt sent as a midsummer gift?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、さっきモンキで」
lines.english: “Nah. Got it at Monki just now.”

lines.japanese: ああ、モンキホーテ。さすが２４時間爆安の殿堂。
lines.english: Ah. Monki Hote. Just what you’d expect from the twenty-four-hour palace of blowout bargains.

lines.japanese: 「こーゆーの、いくらぐらいすんの」
lines.english: “How much does one of these cost?”

lines.japanese: 「知んね」
lines.english: “Dunno.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は値札を探した。どこにも付いてない。代わりに「景品用」というタグが付いていた。
lines.english: I looked for a price tag. There wasn't one. Instead, I found a tag that said PRIZE ITEM.

lines.japanese: 親子連れからお水な兄さん姉さんまで、多様な客層を迎えうる柳木原のモンキホーテ。地階アミューズメントスペースでは、香水から高枝切りバサミまで様々なプライズグッズがゲットできます！
lines.english: The Yanagihara Monki Hote welcomes everyone from families with children to the slick hosts and hostesses of the nightlife trade! Down in its basement arcade, fabulous prizes await, from perfume to telescoping pruning shears!

lines.japanese: はあ。暇だなこいつ。こんな時間まで、ひとりでクレーンゲーム──
lines.english: God. Guy's got time to kill. Playing crane games by himself this late—

lines.japanese: 「──あれ。おまえ、今日はひとりなの」
lines.english: “—wait. You're by yourself today?”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　見りゃ分かんだろ。誰といりゃ満足なんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? You got eyes. Who do I need to be with to make you happy?”

lines.japanese: 森里は腰の下で両手を広げて笑った。笑ったけど、ぴりぴりとした不快感が混じっていた。なんだこいつ、めんどくせえな。
lines.english: Morisato spread both hands low at his sides and laughed, but there was a brittle edge of irritation to it. What the hell? This guy was exhausting.

lines.japanese: 「なんでもいいや、俺には関係ねーし。じゃ仕事戻るわ」
lines.english: “Whatever. Nothing to do with me. I'm going back to work.”

lines.japanese: 「あぁ、おまえさ」
lines.english: “Hey, you.”

lines.japanese: 思いだしたように──と言うよりは、これを忘れてはならないと言った感じで──やつは俺を呼びとめた。
lines.english: As though he'd just remembered—or rather, as though this were the one thing he absolutely could not allow himself to forget—he called me back.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あのさ」
lines.english: “Uh, look.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「あー……やっぱいいわ」
lines.english: “Uh... never mind.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃな」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、ちょーちょーちょー。なんだよ、言えよ気持ち悪りぃな。残尿感たっぷりじゃねーか」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa, whoa. What is it? Say it, you creep. This is like walking away with half a piss still in me.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、まぁ、なんてーか……その、亜衣……なんだけどさ」
lines.english: “Well, it's... you know... Ai.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、香田。香田がなに」
lines.english: “Oh, Koda. What about her?”

lines.japanese: 「なにってほどのことじゃねンだけど……あの、おまえ的にさ、ぶっちゃけあいつどうよ」
lines.english: “It's not a big deal or anything... but, uh, speaking for yourself, honestly, what do you think of her?”

lines.japanese: 「どうってなに。どう、どうなんだよ」
lines.english: “What do I think of her how? What are you asking?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、あんじゃん、たとえばほら……可愛いとか可愛くないとかさあ」
lines.english: “You know. Like... I mean, do you think she's cute or not?”

lines.japanese: 「はァ？　ああ、そっか。あれだろおまえら、またケンカでもしたんだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, I get it. You two had another fight, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、そういうわけじゃねーけど」
lines.english: “It's not like that.”

lines.japanese: 森里は爪先でアスファルトの切れ目をほじくりながら拗ねた声を出す。
lines.english: Morisato spoke in a sulky voice while digging at a crack in the asphalt with his toe.

lines.japanese: 女の愚痴でもこぼしに来たんだろうか。くだらない。ことわざによれば、夫婦喧嘩なんてものはドッグフードよりも不味いと決まっている。俺はさっさとお引き取り願いたく、適当に励ましてやることにした。
lines.english: Had he come to complain about his girl? Pointless. As the old saying had it, a couple’s quarrel tasted worse than dog food. Wanting him gone as soon as possible, I decided to offer some halfhearted encouragement.

lines.japanese: 「んー、香田なあ……人見知りしねーし、言うことアホだけど芯はマトモだし、ああいうのが意外と男に好かれるんだよな。おまえ、ケンカとかしてる余裕ねーだろ。な、さっさと謝って仲良くしとけ？」
lines.english: “Hmm. Koda, huh... She's not shy, and she says some dumb shit, but her head's screwed on straight. Girls like that are surprisingly popular with guys. You don't have time to be fighting with her, do you? Just hurry up, apologize, and make nice, okay?”

lines.japanese: そう言って森里の首にふかふかタオルをかけ、その上から肩にぽんと手を置いてやった。
lines.english: With that, I draped the fluffy towel around Morisato's neck and gave his shoulder a reassuring pat through it.

lines.japanese: 「さわるな？」
lines.english: “Don't touch me, okay?”

lines.japanese: やつは首を傾げてにっこり笑いながら、肩のフケでも落とすように俺の手を払いのけた。自分から聞いてきたくせして、なに照れてんだこいつ。
lines.english: Tilting his head with a bright smile, he brushed off my hand as though flicking dandruff from his shoulder. He was the one who'd asked, so what the hell was he getting embarrassed about?

lines.japanese: 「あ～あ……ほんじゃなー、また来るわー」
lines.english: “Aaaah, well... See you. I'll come by again.”

lines.japanese: 「おー」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや。来なくていいから」
lines.english: “No, no, no. You don't need to come back.”

lines.japanese: 俺は遠ざかる背中に慌てて手を伸ばした。やつは顧みず、手を振るようにタオルを空に放った。
lines.english: I hurriedly reached toward his retreating back. Without looking around, he flung the towel into the air in lieu of a wave.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや。捨てんならよそで捨てろっつーの。ポイ捨て禁止条例なめんな。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “No, no, no. If you're gonna throw it away, do it somewhere else. Don't fuck with the anti-littering ordinance. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: しかし俺の立場上、路上の投棄物を見過ごすわけにもいかず、仕方なくとぼとぼ歩いていってそれを拾いあげた。
lines.english: But in my position, I couldn't ignore trash dumped in the street. I trudged over and reluctantly picked it up.

lines.japanese: 意味分かんねえ。もっと分かりやすいバカだったのに、なんかあいつ、だんだんバカさ加減が大将に似てきてねえか？
lines.english: Made no sense. He used to be a much more straightforward kind of idiot. Was he starting to take after the boss even in how stupid he was?

lines.japanese: 「あと、髪切れ髪」
lines.english: “And cut your hair.”

lines.japanese: 俺はタオルを肩にかけ、遠ざかる背中に二本指を突きつけた。目潰しピース。
lines.english: I slung the towel over my shoulder and jabbed two fingers toward his retreating back. The Eye-Gouging Peace Sign.
